chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: The Four Dots and the Harlem Highlanders
summary: He recalls the Four Dots in Washington and playing piano with the Harlem Highlanders, then reviving the act around 1951.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Among other accounts of your early days as a musician I saw mention of a group called the Four Dots,

That was my guitar beginning, because they would be practicin', rehearsin', you know, and they were all guitars... Let's see I may be gettin' a couple groups mixed up. The 4 Dots I think were from Washington, and we used to hang out together. But I believe it was the Harlem Highlenders that's where I met Snags Allen and I used to listen to them fellas rehearse.
Did you play with the Harlem Highlenders?

Yeah, I used to play piano off and on now and then you know. Always used to hang out together. They had a week of a group. A whole show, man. Singin', dancin, with Baby Lawrence and a couple of other dancers, and all of 'em could sing like the... Merrimacks, I believe you'd call it, at that time Tommy Dorsey had a group called the Modernaires I believe. And they could sing like that, then they could dance and play music off on top of it. It was somethin' else.

Well at that time I wasn't a member. Later on, a few years later, I thought about this act. I said, 'why couldn't that act go over.' 'Cause it was a million-dollar act, they just didn't have the right manager, or agent. So I think it was 1951 -- I tried to revive it. And we went over good, you know. But still couldn't find a good manager behind us. Man it was a sight to see the bag.
